{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Julia Elisenda''' ('''Eli''') '''Grigsby''' is an American mathematician who works as a professor at [[Boston College]].{{r|cv}} Her research began with the study of [[low-dimensional topology]], including [[knot theory]] and [[category theory|category-theoretic]] [[knot invariant]]s.{{r|birman|notices}}  She is currently working in the field of machine learning.

==Education and career==
Grigsby earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics from [[Harvard University]] in 1999,{{r|cv|birman}} after earlier forays into biochemistry and physics. After a year working as an [[operations research]]er in [[Silicon Valley]], she returned to graduate school at the [[University of California, Berkeley]],{{r|notices}} and completed her doctorate in 2005 under the joint supervision of [[Robion Kirby]] and [[Peter Ozsváth]].{{r|cv|birman|mgp}}

She was a postdoctoral researcher at [[Columbia University]] and the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]], and joined the Boston College faculty in 2009.{{r|cv}}

==Service==
Grigsby belongs to the advisory board of Girls' Angle, a non-profit organization for encouraging girls to participate in mathematics,{{r|cv|angle}} and is responsible for creating a sequence of video lectures by women in mathematics for Girls' Angle.{{r|angle}}

==Recognition==
In 2014 she became the inaugural winner of the [[Joan & Joseph Birman Research Prize in Topology and Geometry]], given biennially by the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] to an outstanding early-career female researcher in topology and geometry.{{r|birman}}
